evidence.quote: Ventura County Credit Union ("Owner")

evidence.quote: the project known as the Oxnard Branch Remodel
evidence.rationale: Recital names the Project.

evidence.quote: This Subcontract shall be governed by the laws of the State of California.
evidence.rationale: Section 12.10 governing law clause.

evidence.quote: This Section governs the timing of payment and does not make Owner's payment a condition to Contractor's ultimate obligation to pay for Work properly performed.
evidence.rationale: Section 13.4 calls itself a pay-when-paid timing provision and expressly says Owner payment is not a condition to Contractor's ultimate obligation. However, its first sentence says payment is "conditioned on" Owner payment, so classification requires reading the clause as a whole.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay Subcontractor the amount due within seven (7) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for that Work.
evidence.rationale: Section 13.4 states seven days after receipt of Owner payment.

evidence.quote: The parties have agreed to this pay-when-paid timing provision in writing by signing this Subcontract.
evidence.rationale: A specific period is written into Section 13.4, and the parties expressly acknowledge written agreement.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall withhold retention of five percent (5%) from each progress payment to Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Section 13.5 states 5% retention, which is 500 bps.

release_condition.value: upon Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner; subject to Subcontractor's delivery of all closeout documents, warranties, and final lien waivers

evidence.quote: Retention shall become due upon Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Section 13.6 sets two conditions plus a closeout-document proviso. Final Completion is defined (1.3) to require acceptance by Contractor, Architect and Owner, so the clauses must be combined.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay the retention to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after both conditions have been satisfied
evidence.rationale: Section 13.6 states ten days after both conditions are satisfied.

evidence.quote: As a condition of each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver with its application a conditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount requested
evidence.rationale: Section 13.8 requires a conditional progress waiver with each application.

evidence.quote: within ten (10) days after receipt of each payment shall deliver an unconditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount received
evidence.rationale: Section 13.8 requires an unconditional waiver within 10 days after each payment.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall also obtain and deliver, with each application, conditional and unconditional waivers on the same statutory forms from each Lower-Tier Party
evidence.rationale: Section 13.8 requires waivers from Lower-Tier Parties with each application.

evidence.quote: All waivers shall be executed on the statutory forms set forth in California Civil Code Sections 8132, 8134, 8136, and 8138, as applicable, and no other form shall be accepted.
evidence.rationale: Section 13.8 mandates the California statutory forms.

evidence.quote: Contractor may set off against any amount due Subcontractor under this Subcontract all backcharges, costs, and damages for which Subcontractor is liable to Contractor
evidence.rationale: Section 13.7 grants a setoff right for backcharges, costs and damages.

evidence.quote: (a) defective or nonconforming Work that has not been corrected, in an amount up to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the reasonable estimated cost of correction
evidence.rationale: Section 13.7 permits withholding for uncorrected defective Work and for claims, liens and stop payment notices.

evidence.quote: Contractor will not pay for materials or equipment that are stored on or off the Site and not yet incorporated into the Work; applications for payment shall include only installed Work.
evidence.rationale: Section 13.3 expressly excludes stored materials on or off site.

anomalies.description: Section 13.4 opens with condition-precedent language (payment "conditioned on" Owner payment) that reads like pay-if-paid. The same section then disclaims that Owner payment is a condition to Contractor's ultimate obligation. This internal tension should be reviewed before relying on the pay-when-paid classification.

evidence.quote: Payment to Subcontractor is conditioned on Contractor's receipt of payment from Owner for the Work covered by the application.
evidence.rationale: Section 13.4 opens with condition-precedent language (payment "conditioned on" Owner payment) that reads like pay-if-paid. The same section then disclaims that Owner payment is a condition to Contractor's ultimate obligation. This internal tension should be reviewed before relying on the pay-when-paid classification.

anomalies.description: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. It also depends on Final Completion, which is defined to require acceptance by Contractor, Architect and Owner, and on delivery of closeout documents. Release timing is therefore tied to Owner and to third-party acceptance.

evidence.quote: Retention shall become due upon Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. It also depends on Final Completion, which is defined to require acceptance by Contractor, Architect and Owner, and on delivery of closeout documents. Release timing is therefore tied to Owner and to third-party acceptance.

anomalies.description: Final Completion requires acceptance by Contractor, Architect and Owner, which is a discretionary trigger for retention release.

evidence.quote: has been completed and accepted by Contractor, Architect, and Owner
evidence.rationale: Final Completion requires acceptance by Contractor, Architect and Owner, which is a discretionary trigger for retention release.

evidence.rationale: Contractor may withhold up to 150% of the estimated correction cost for defective Work. It may also withhold for merely "reasonably threatened" Lower-Tier claims and on "reasonable evidence" the Work cannot be completed for the unpaid balance.

anomalies.description: Setoff applies against any amount due under the Subcontract, which could include retention. The setoff covers all backcharges, costs and damages, including cleanup, supplementation and completion costs.

evidence.rationale: Setoff applies against any amount due under the Subcontract, which could include retention. The setoff covers all backcharges, costs and damages, including cleanup, supplementation and completion costs.

anomalies.description: Contractor may purchase insurance Subcontractor fails to maintain and deduct its cost from amounts due. This is an additional deduction right outside Article 13.

evidence.quote: Contractor may, without obligation, purchase that insurance and deduct the cost from amounts due Subcontractor
evidence.rationale: Contractor may purchase insurance Subcontractor fails to maintain and deduct its cost from amounts due. This is an additional deduction right outside Article 13.

anomalies.description: Contractor may unilaterally adjust payment applications based on its own assessment before passing them to Owner, which is a discretionary reduction of billed amounts.

evidence.quote: Contractor may adjust the application to reflect its assessment of the Work actually completed and then include it in Contractor's application to Owner.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may unilaterally adjust payment applications based on its own assessment before passing them to Owner, which is a discretionary reduction of billed amounts.

anomalies.description: Applications are due by the 20th but must cover Work completed through the end of that month. Subcontractor is therefore billing projected Work not yet performed at submission.

evidence.quote: On or before the 20th day of each month, Subcontractor shall submit to Contractor an application for payment covering Work completed through the end of that month
evidence.rationale: Applications are due by the 20th but must cover Work completed through the end of that month. Subcontractor is therefore billing projected Work not yet performed at submission.

anomalies.description: Several clauses pass Owner payment risk to Subcontractor on specific items. Delay compensation is limited to amounts Owner actually pays. Change adjustments are limited to what Owner allows. Termination recovery is capped at Owner payments when Owner terminates. Owner-related claims are paid only after Owner pays.

evidence.quote: together with any monetary compensation that Owner actually pays to Contractor on account of Subcontractor's delay claim, less Contractor's reasonable costs of pursuing it.
evidence.rationale: Several clauses pass Owner payment risk to Subcontractor on specific items. Delay compensation is limited to amounts Owner actually pays. Change adjustments are limited to what Owner allows. Termination recovery is capped at Owner payments when Owner terminates. Owner-related claims are paid only after Owner pays.

anomalies.description: If Owner terminates the Prime Contract, Subcontractor's recovery is capped at what Owner pays Contractor for the Subcontract Work.

evidence.quote: If Owner terminates the Prime Contract, Subcontractor's recovery shall not exceed the amount Owner pays Contractor on account of the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: If Owner terminates the Prime Contract, Subcontractor's recovery is capped at what Owner pays Contractor for the Subcontract Work.

anomalies.description: Each application must include both conditional and unconditional statutory waivers from every Lower-Tier Party, covering the current application and prior payments. This is a heavy administrative condition to payment.

evidence.rationale: Each application must include both conditional and unconditional statutory waivers from every Lower-Tier Party, covering the current application and prior payments. This is a heavy administrative condition to payment.
